title: Mahdi
tagline: Service booking app connecting a local business with its customers, backed by a Laravel API.
overview: Mahdi is a service booking app I built early in my Flutter journey, pairing a Flutter client with a Laravel backend to let customers browse and book services from a local business.
problem: The business was managing bookings manually through phone calls and messages, making it hard to track availability or avoid double-booking.
solution: A Flutter app for browsing available services and time slots, backed by a Laravel API that manages availability, bookings, and basic customer records.
architecture: Flutter app communicating with a Laravel REST API over authenticated endpoints, with a MySQL database modeling services, time slots, and bookings.
features: Service catalog with availability by time slot
challenges: Modeling availability and preventing double-bookings correctly at the database level
This was one of my earliest Flutter and Laravel integrations, so establishing clean API contracts took real iteration
lessonsLearned: Getting the booking/availability data model right from the start avoids a lot of downstream edge-case bugs
futureImprovements: Calendar sync for the business owner
results: Replaced manual phone-based booking with a structured digital flow
